subject: APAC activation window for subprocessor onboarding — residency impact?
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@avasys.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@avasys.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC activation window for subprocessor onboarding — residency impact?

Hi Monica,

We are preparing to onboard a new analytics subprocessor in APAC as part of our Dedicated deployment. The vendor needs an activation window for their agent pool (they estimate ~1-4 hours) during which some traffic may be routed through a warm-up control plane. Before we proceed I need explicit confirmation about two things:

1) Will any customer content originating in APAC be routed to or buffered in US-hosted systems during the vendor activation? If so, what is the maximum expected transient window and where would the data be stored (region/KMS)?
2) Can Redwood provide SOC 2/ISA evidence for the subprocessor and an ingestion runbook excerpt showing the activation steps, so our security team can sign off?

We are particularly sensitive about PHI-adjacent telemetry and would like to avoid any permanent cross-border residency changes. If there is a short transient window we need this captured in an addendum to our DPA with specific maximum duration and audit log requirements.

Attached is a simple roster of the subprocessor ask. Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam Chen
Head of Platform Security, Ava Systems
liam.chen@avasys.com
Attachment: ava-subprocessor-request-20270420.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@avasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal@avasys.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC activation window for subprocessor onboarding — residency impact?

Thanks Liam — good questions. Short summary up front: we can support APAC pinning without permanent cross-border residency, and we have operational mitigations that avoid uncontrolled buffering in US by default. That said, certain activation workflows may temporarily traverse control plane infrastructure outside APAC for orchestration, and we want to be explicit about the bounds.

Key points / proposed commitments:
- Region-local data plane: All inference/customer payloads are served from APAC GPU pools once a model variant is pinned to APAC.
- Activation choreography: During subprocessor agent activation we may perform brief health checks and artifact validation that touch our control plane services. We do not persist customer payloads in US object stores as part of that process.
- Transient buffering window: Our engineering ops recommends a maximum technical window of 0-4 hours for activation-related orchestration, with typical activations completing in under 30 minutes. We can commit to a customer-facing contractual cap of 48 hours for any exceptional transient processing, with notification and post-hoc audit logs.
- KMS locality: By default KMS keys associated with APAC customers remain in the APAC region. If a cross-region operation is required we can log a KMS key-wrap event and surface it in audit logs.
- Evidence: I'm attaching our APAC Onboarding Playbook excerpt and can provide a SOC 2 summary for the specific subprocessor (pending vendor consent).

Next steps I propose:
1) Engineering to confirm whether activation artifacts ever traverse US object storage and provide the runbook snippet. @karthik_iyer can you confirm?
2) Security/legal to draft DPA amendment language limiting transient cross-border buffering to 48 hours with required audit log fields. @marissa_cole / @markus_klein — can you take this?
3) If helpful, schedule a 30 minute call with the Ava security team to walk the runbook and sample logs.

Happy to sync this afternoon if schedules line up.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-apac-onboarding-playbook.pdf

Monica — appreciated. A few follow-ups from our legal/security review:

- The 48-hour contractual cap is acceptable in principle, but Ava needs the DPA addendum to include: the exact audit fields that will be produced (timestamp, event-type, resource-id, source-region, destination-region, key-id), retention period for those logs, and the method for customer retrieval (S3 export or portal API).
- Can you provide a sanitized sample of the activation runbook (we only need the orchestration steps that touch control plane services) and a one-week sample of audit log entries showing a previous activation (redacted identifiers) so our team can validate the coverage?
- Confirm KMS behavior: if a KMS wrap occurs during activation, does Redwood generate a distinct key-wrap audit event with the wrapped key-id and region?

If you can deliver the runbook snippet + sample logs and a proposed DPA amendment draft we can move to a quick legal review and sign the addendum. Otherwise we'll pause subprocessor go-live.

Thanks — can we assume a 48-hour SLA to get these artifacts?

Liam
--
Liam Chen
Head of Platform Security, Ava Systems

Folks — looping you in with Ava. Action items below, we need to move fast to keep the deal timeline:

Action items
- @karthik_iyer: Provide a runbook snippet (or sanitized excerpt) of the activation choreography and confirm whether any activation artifacts are ever stored in US object stores. Please include typical and worst-case activation durations. Target: 48 hours.
- @marissa_cole: Draft DPA addendum language that: (a) sets a 48-hour contractual cap for exceptional transient cross-border buffering, (b) enumerates required audit fields (timestamp, event-type, resource-id, source-region, destination-region, key-id), and (c) specifies log retrieval method and retention (we typically provide 90 days via export).
- @markus_klein: Pull a redacted sample (7-day window) of activation audit logs and a SOC2 summary for the named subprocessor; confirm consent to share vendor SOC2. If vendor consents not yet obtained, note that in the response.
- @marissa_cole / legal: Prepare a short DocuSign addendum template we can send to Ava for signature. Link to draft: https://docusign.com/rafts/AVA-ADDENDUM-20270421

I'll coordinate the customer call once we have the runbook + logs. Please treat this as high priority for the next 48 business hours.

Thanks,
Monica
